source: Somsak Wannasaree, "Banana Orchards" (Khmer translation, 1997), section 12 (packing for transport)
text:
For fruit destined for more distant markets, this source describes packing hands/clusters into cardboard cartons lined with protective paper (historically newspaper) to cushion the fruit against bruising, with box weights in the range the source describes as roughly 12.5kg per carton — a figure that lines up closely with the 14kg-per-carton standard seen in more recent Cambodia-to-China export shipping documents.

An important practical note for anyone pricing or planning shipments: the source cites a typical weight loss of around 7.8% of a box's weight over the course of a long-distance shipment, caused mainly by moisture loss from the fruit during transit. This is worth factoring into pricing and contract terms, since a box weighed and priced at origin will typically arrive lighter, and buyers accustomed to export trade generally expect and account for some shrinkage of this kind rather than treating it as a defect.

Good carton ventilation, appropriate humidity control, and minimizing the total time and handling between packing and delivery all help reduce this loss and reduce bruising damage in transit.
